# Author controlled technical English

Use this skill for a technical document in any project.
Read [the source map](../../../docs/asd-ste100-issue9.md).
Use an authorized copy of ASD-STE100 Issue 9 when you check approved words.
Do not assume that this skill replaces the full standard.

## Procedure

1. Identify the reader, purpose, and subject field.
2. Identify whether the text gives instructions or describes a system.
3. For instructions, give one action in each sentence.
4. Put a required condition before its action.
5. Use the active voice and a clear verb.
6. Use the approved meanings and parts of speech from the Issue 9 dictionary.
7. For a technical noun or verb, use a term approved in the subject field.
8. Use the same technical term for the same concept.
9. Keep procedure sentences to a maximum of 20 words.
10. Keep description sentences to a maximum of 25 words.
11. Keep descriptive paragraphs to a maximum of six sentences.
12. Use a list when it makes steps or parts easier to read.
13. Do not change exact identifiers, command text, code, or quoted output.
14. Run the [review tool](../../../scripts/ste-review.mjs).
15. Correct tool findings and complete a manual dictionary and rule review.

## Output

Report the source edition.
Give the text and the review result.
If the dictionary review did not occur, mark the result **Partial review**.
Do not claim complete ASD-STE100 compliance from a word-count check alone.
